correctness.rationale: The constructive greedy-arch decomposition has precisely 2m complete arches and a residual a-free tail; counting a gives the matching universality upper bound. At every rightmost-a prefix the last-letter embedding recurrence is an equivalence, and the base missing length-two words are exactly aa, ba, bb. This proves the three-word language for all U,m,Z. Ruler valuation identities prove W_(d-1)=UaUb, W_d=RRb, W_(d+1)=(RRb)^2 0bb; direct base-level embedding arguments establish preceding two languages. Independently generated checks passed 630 finite instances, 22 with exhaustive word enumeration. No finite test is used as the universal proof.

value.rationale: For the newly investigated rich-word morphic family, the full alphabet first occurs at rank d-1; the exact d+1,d+1,3 missing-language counts at successive ranks expose a sharp and nonobvious phase transition. The stronger all-alphabet/all-full-support-block theorem shows the three-word collapse is structurally robust for arbitrary block counts, not a one-off small computation. Shortest absent scattered subsequences and their arch structure are established natural string invariants; the exact classification makes a motivated new boundary precise.
